"# llama.cpp for Apple Silicon Research

## Installation and Setup Process

### Prerequisites
- Xcode Command Line Tools
- CMake (can be installed via Homebrew: `brew install cmake`)
- Git

### Installation Steps
1. Clone the repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp.git
   cd llama.cpp
   ```

2. Build with Metal support:
   ```bash
   mkdir build
   cd build
   cmake .. -DLLAMA_METAL=ON
   cmake --build . --config Release
   ```

3. Download a compatible model (e.g., Llama 2):
   - Models can be downloaded from Hugging Face or converted from Meta's releases
   - Convert using the provided conversion scripts:
     ```bash
     python convert.py --outfile models/7B/ggml-model-f16.bin --outtype f16 /path/to/llama/model
     ```

4. Run inference:
   ```bash
   ./bin/main -m models/7B/ggml-model-f16.bin -n 128
   ```

## Inference Capabilities and Performance Benchmarks

### Performance on Apple Silicon
- M1 Pro/Max: ~30 tokens/sec for 7B models (4-bit quantized)
- M2 Pro/Max: ~40 tokens/sec for 7B models (4-bit quantized)
- M3 Pro/Max: ~50-60 tokens/sec for 7B models (4-bit quantized)

### Memory Usage
- 7B model (4-bit quantized): ~4GB RAM
- 13B model (4-bit quantized): ~8GB RAM
- 70B model (4-bit quantized): ~35GB RAM

### Context Length
- Default: 2048 tokens
- Extendable up to 32K tokens (depending on model and available memory)

### Metal vs. CPU Performance
- Metal acceleration provides 3-5x speedup over CPU-only inference
- Batch processing particularly benefits from Metal acceleration

## Quantization Methods Supported

### Supported Quantization Types
- Q4_0: 4-bit integer quantization (legacy)
- Q4_1: 4-bit integer quantization with higher accuracy
- Q5_0: 5-bit integer quantization
- Q5_1: Improved 5-bit quantization
- Q8_0: 8-bit integer quantization
- F16: Half-precision floating point (no quantization)

### Quantization Process
1. Convert the original model to GGML format
2. Apply quantization during conversion:
   ```bash
   python convert.py --outfile models/7B/ggml-model-q4_0.bin --outtype q4_0 /path/to/model
   ```

### Quantization Impact
- Q4_0: ~75% size reduction, minimal quality loss
- Q5_0: ~69% size reduction, very minor quality loss
- Q8_0: ~50% size reduction, negligible quality loss

## Fine-tuning Approaches

### LoRA Fine-tuning
- Supports Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning
- Significantly reduces memory requirements compared to full fine-tuning
- Implementation available in the repository

### Fine-tuning Process
1. Prepare training data in the correct format
2. Run fine-tuning script with appropriate parameters:
   ```bash
   ./finetune --model-base ./models/7B/ggml-model-q4_0.bin --lora-out ./lora-out --train-data ./train-data.txt
   ```

3. Apply LoRA adapters during inference:
   ```bash
   ./main -m ./models/7B/ggml-model-q4_0.bin --lora ./lora-out -p "Your prompt here"
   ```

### Limitations
- Full fine-tuning not supported in llama.cpp (only LoRA)
- Training on Apple Silicon is less optimized than inference
- Limited hyperparameter tuning options compared to PyTorch implementations

## Integration with Apple's Metal Framework

### Metal Implementation
- Uses Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) for optimized matrix multiplication
- Custom Metal compute kernels for specific operations
- Automatic Metal device selection on multi-GPU systems

### Configuration Options
- Enable Metal: `-DLLAMA_METAL=ON` during CMake configuration
- Control Metal usage: `--metal` flag at runtime
- Limit memory usage: `--metal-memory N` (where N is in MB)

### Best Practices for Metal
- Keep batch sizes moderate (1-8) for optimal performance
- Ensure sufficient free GPU memory before inference
- For multi-GPU systems, set `--metal-device N` to select specific GPU
- Use Metal Performance HUD to monitor GPU utilization

## Recent Developments

### Metal Optimizations
- New tensor splitting algorithms for handling larger models
- Improved memory management for Metal buffers
- Optimized kernels for M3 series chips

### Community Extensions
- Various UI implementations (including native macOS apps)
- Server implementations for API access
- Integration with other frameworks like LangChain"
